source.title: Are SAE features from the Base Model still meaningful to LLaVA?

record.tranche_reason: Tests transfer of text-trained SAE features in a multimodal model, a new setting, using feature retrieval and classification rather than the original toy-model setup.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE-feature occurrences and classification outcomes, so these are included. The 1000-occurrence cutoff is a cleaning choice, not a result. The quoted ImageNet-1k result is included as a separate result; the authors say that experiment was still running.
record.test_reason: The study applies Gemma-trained SAEs to image-patch tokens of a multimodal LLaVA-Gemma model. It reports whether class-aligned sparse features are recovered at each layer, which bears on V4 in a new setting. The classification experiments mainly compare the study's own pipeline settings.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say base-model SAE features generalize to LLaVA, recovering nearly 100% of ViT performance. They say middle-layer, binarized, larger feature sets work best, including with little data. They frame the work as in-progress lab-meeting material, and report that deeper layers (0–12) yield increasingly useful retrieved features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained SAEs to extract features from a multimodal model and evaluates them with feature inspection and linear classification; it does not use the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by layer, feature budget, activation binarization, and training-data amount; the 12-it feature examples use an instruct-model-trained SAE.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-trained SAE features applied to LLaVA image tokens support linear CIFAR-100 classification described as near the ViT's 0.85 Macro F1. Results depend on layer (10 best), feature budget and binarization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features transfer across modalities (base text model to multimodal model) and retain task-relevant information.

record.problems: The post describes the work as exploratory and in progress. Most SAE classification comparisons have no exact scores or uncertainty estimates. Feature descriptions are qualitative, only one multimodal model and CIFAR-100 are tested, and the ImageNet-1k experiment is described as still running.

untested.parts: Toy-model geometry, sparsity transition and regular geometry: not studied.
Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity: not studied.
Non-capacity causes of polysemanticity: not studied.
Whether features are distributed across many neurons; SAE reconstruction quality or sparsity in LLaVA; any SAE trained on LLaVA itself.
Completeness and canonicity of SAE features. Cross-modal transfer hints at stability but is not measured as such.

missing.what: Exact Macro F1 values per layer, pooling method, binarization and data split, shown only in figures ('Binaired feature helps', data-efficiency plot).
missing.versions: none (method performance); needed to check r21–r28

record.verdict_notes: V4 evidence is qualitative. It rests on authors' auto-interp labels of the top-2 features per class per layer, for only 4 hand-picked classes, with no random or control baseline. The top-feature counts follow a 1000-occurrence cleaning filter. The 'boy' features focus on clothing and parenting, which the authors themselves remark on.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity or causes important features to receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure.

The study tests transfer and task utility of SAE features in one multimodal model and classification task; it does not measure how broadly features are distributed across neurons or establish recovery across LLMs generally.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

statements.correction: This study transfers pretrained Gemma SAEs to LLaVA and includes an instruct-trained SAE at layer 12; it reports no matched preference/RL comparison or trajectory through training stages.
